title: MOH UAE
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public MOH UAE health-professional examination syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A 58-year-old man presents with crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm and is clammy and short of breath. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?
options: Obtain a 12-lead ECG and start continuous cardiac monitoring while escalating urgently
Administer oral ibuprofen and ask the patient to walk to assess the pain
Reassure the patient and schedule an outpatient cardiology appointment
Delay assessment until the patient has finished his meal
items.explanation: Suspected acute coronary syndrome is time-critical, so immediate ECG, monitoring and urgent escalation are required. Analgesia alone, mobilisation, delay or outpatient planning all forfeit the reperfusion window.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with type 1 diabetes has a capillary glucose of 3.1 mmol/L and is sweaty and confused but able to swallow. What should the nurse do first?
options: Administer the next scheduled dose of long-acting insulin
Give 15 to 20 g of fast-acting oral carbohydrate and recheck glucose shortly
Withhold all oral intake and wait for the medical team
Document the finding and recheck the glucose after one hour
items.explanation: This is hypoglycaemia in a conscious patient, so fast-acting carbohydrate is first-line. Giving insulin worsens it, and withholding treatment or delaying a recheck risks neuroglycopenic harm.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with an acute asthma attack is using accessory muscles, cannot complete sentences, and has an oxygen saturation of 89% on room air. What is the priority action?
options: Lay the patient flat and withhold bronchodilators until reviewed
Give an oral sedative to reduce the work of breathing
Sit the patient upright, give oxygen to target saturation, and administer a nebulised bronchodilator
Send the patient for a chest radiograph before starting any treatment
items.explanation: A severe asthma attack needs upright positioning, oxygen and prompt bronchodilation. Lying flat impairs ventilation, sedatives are dangerous in respiratory failure, and delaying treatment for imaging is unsafe.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: An older patient admitted with pneumonia now has a respiratory rate of 30, new confusion, and a blood pressure of 88/54 mmHg. What does this constellation most suggest?
options: A mild self-limiting viral illness suitable for discharge
Simple anxiety needing only reassurance
Stable chronic angina needing routine review
Sepsis requiring urgent assessment and escalation
items.explanation: Tachypnoea, altered mentation and hypotension after infection point to sepsis and demand urgent escalation. The other options underestimate a red-flag presentation and would delay time-critical treatment.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient recovering from a stroke develops new facial droop and arm weakness, with a last known well time of about ninety minutes earlier. What is the priority?
options: Activate the stroke pathway and arrange urgent brain imaging
Document the findings and reassess at the next round
Give the patient a hot drink and encourage mobilisation
Await the routine weekly neurology review
items.explanation: New neurological deficit within the thrombolysis window is an emergency, so the stroke pathway and urgent imaging are essential. Observation, oral intake and delayed review all miss the treatment window.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with known heart failure reports new breathlessness when lying flat and has gained 2 kg over three days. What should the nurse do?
options: Reassure the patient that weight gain is expected and take no action
Assess the fluid status and escalate to the medical team for review
Remove the prescribed diuretic from the medication chart
Encourage the patient to increase oral fluid intake
items.explanation: Orthopnoea and rapid weight gain suggest fluid overload and decompensation, so assessment and escalation are required. Ignoring it, stopping a diuretic, or pushing fluids would worsen the failure.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with an acute exacerbation of COPD is prescribed controlled oxygen therapy. What is the appropriate target oxygen saturation range?
options: 94 to 98 percent
Above 98 percent regardless of history
88 to 92 percent
Below 85 percent to avoid carbon dioxide retention
items.explanation: In COPD at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure the target is 88 to 92 percent. Higher targets risk carbon dioxide retention, and deliberately aiming below 85 percent causes hypoxaemia.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with a suspected upper gastrointestinal bleed has a heart rate of 118, a blood pressure of 88/54 mmHg, and cool peripheries. What is the priority action?
options: Give oral iron tablets to correct the anaemia immediately
Allow a large meal to settle the stomach
Arrange discharge with a follow-up clinic appointment
Initiate resuscitative measures and escalate urgently for possible transfusion
items.explanation: Shock after a suspected bleed requires resuscitation and urgent escalation for blood products. Oral iron is slow, feeding is inappropriate in an acute bleed, and discharge would be dangerous.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with diabetes is scheduled for elective surgery. Which preoperative nursing action is most important?
options: Confirm fasting status and manage glucose according to the agreed protocol
Give a large dose of insulin without first checking the glucose
Allow unlimited sugary drinks up to the time of surgery
Omit all diabetes medication without informing the team
items.explanation: Safe perioperative care requires confirming fasting and following the glucose-management protocol. Unchecked insulin, sugary drinks and silent omission of medication all risk hypo or hyperglycaemia.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient has a suspected deep vein thrombosis with a swollen, painful calf. Which nursing action should be avoided?
options: Measuring and documenting the calf circumference
Vigorous massage of the affected leg
Elevating the leg as tolerated
Escalating for assessment and possible anticoagulation
items.explanation: Massaging a suspected DVT may dislodge a thrombus and cause pulmonary embolism, so it must be avoided. Measuring, elevating and escalating for anticoagulation are appropriate and safe.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: Over six hours a patient has produced only 120 mL of urine and the serum creatinine has risen. What does this most suggest?
options: Excellent hydration with normal renal function
A normal finding that requires no action
Acute kidney injury requiring review and possible fluid management
Diabetes insipidus with excessive urine output
items.explanation: Oliguria with a rising creatinine indicates acute kidney injury and needs prompt review and fluid assessment. Normal-function claims ignore the data, while diabetes insipidus presents with large urine volumes, not oliguria.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient recovering from chemotherapy develops a temperature of 38.3 degrees Celsius with a low neutrophil count. What is the priority?
options: Give paracetamol and observe for 24 hours
Wait for the next scheduled blood test before acting
Advise the patient to manage the fever at home
Treat it as a medical emergency and follow the neutropenic sepsis protocol
items.explanation: Febrile neutropenia is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate protocol-driven treatment. Observation, delay, or home management in this immunosuppressed state risks rapid deterioration and death.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: An older adult becomes acutely confused on the ward. What is the best first step to identify delirium?
options: Assess for acute onset with a fluctuating course and look for an underlying cause
Assume it is dementia and take no further action
Restrain the patient immediately to keep them safe
Arrange transfer to a nursing home the same day
items.explanation: Delirium is an acute, fluctuating disturbance that demands a search for a reversible cause. Labelling it dementia, restraining first, or immediate placement misses a treatable medical problem.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient describes a sudden severe headache as the worst of his life, with neck stiffness and photophobia. What is the main concern?
options: A tension headache suitable for simple analgesia and discharge
Possible subarachnoid haemorrhage requiring urgent investigation
Sinusitis needing a decongestant
A migraine that only needs a triptan
items.explanation: A thunderclap headache with meningism suggests subarachnoid haemorrhage and needs urgent investigation. Treating it as tension headache, sinusitis or migraine delays diagnosis of a life-threatening bleed.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with diabetes is found unconscious and is suspected of being hypoglycaemic. What is the appropriate first-line treatment?
options: Give oral glucose tablets while the patient is unconscious
Administer a dose of rapid-acting insulin
Administer intravenous glucose or glucagon per protocol while monitoring
Withhold treatment and observe the patient
items.explanation: An unconscious patient cannot swallow safely, so parenteral glucose or glucagon is required. Oral glucose risks aspiration, insulin deepens the hypoglycaemia, and withholding treatment can cause brain injury.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A nurse is preparing intravenous insulin, a high-alert medication, for administration. Which safety practice is essential?
options: Reliance on the prescriber alone to check the calculated dose
Estimating the dose by eye to save time
Preparing the syringe in advance and leaving it unlabelled
An independent double-check by a second qualified practitioner before administration
items.explanation: High-alert medications require an independent double-check to catch errors that could be fatal. Unverified prescribing, estimation and unlabelled syringes are all recognised causes of serious medication incidents.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient taking warfarin has an INR of 6.5 and is not currently bleeding. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Withhold the dose and escalate urgently according to the anticoagulation protocol
Administer the usual dose because the result is unimportant
Give an additional dose to stabilise the level
Ignore the result because INR is only relevant after bleeding
items.explanation: A markedly elevated INR carries a high bleeding risk, so the dose is withheld and the protocol followed. Continuing or adding warfarin raises the risk further, and ignoring the INR is unsafe.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient is receiving intravenous gentamicin. Which monitoring is required to detect toxicity?
options: No monitoring because aminoglycosides are free of toxicity
Monitoring renal function and drug levels according to the protocol
Monitoring only for a skin rash
Monitoring blood glucose alone
items.explanation: Aminoglycosides are nephrotoxic and ototoxic, so renal function and levels must be monitored. Claiming no toxicity is false, and rash or glucose monitoring alone would miss kidney and hearing damage.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient receiving intravenous opioids becomes difficult to rouse with a respiratory rate of 8 per minute. What is the priority action?
options: Administer another dose to maintain analgesia
Encourage the patient to sleep it off
Stop the opioid, support the airway, monitor, and consider naloxone per protocol
Increase the infusion rate to keep the line patent
items.explanation: This is opioid-induced respiratory depression, so the opioid is stopped, ventilation supported, and the reversal agent considered. More opioid or a higher rate worsens sedation, and allowing sleep risks respiratory arrest.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A nurse is about to administer a prescribed medicine. Which set of checks reflects the rights of medication administration?
options: Right patient and right drug only
Right cost and right brand name
Right bed number only
Right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, and right time
items.explanation: The classic rights cover patient, drug, dose, route and time, and prevent the majority of administration errors. Partial, commercial or bed-number checks are not valid safeguards for the individual patient.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient with a documented penicillin allergy has been prescribed amoxicillin. What should the nurse do?
options: Clarify with the prescriber before administration because of the documented allergy
Administer the drug as prescribed regardless of the allergy
Give half the usual dose to reduce the risk
Administer it and document the allergy afterwards
items.explanation: A known allergy makes administration unsafe, so the order must be clarified first. Giving the full or half dose risks anaphylaxis, and documenting only afterwards exposes the patient unnecessarily.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient taking digoxin reports nausea and visual disturbance and has a pulse of 48 beats per minute. What does this suggest?
options: A normal therapeutic response to digoxin
Possible digoxin toxicity requiring urgent review of levels and electrolytes
An allergic reaction to a food item only
A need to increase the digoxin dose
items.explanation: Nausea, visual disturbance and bradycardia are classic signs of digoxin toxicity, which can be fatal. Calling it normal or increasing the dose would worsen toxicity, while a food allergy does not explain bradycardia.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient has been started on lithium therapy. Which advice is most important to give?
options: Follow a strict low-salt crash diet to lose weight
Skip monitoring because lithium has a wide safety margin
Attend for regular lithium level checks and keep fluid and salt intake consistent
Take a double dose whenever a dose is missed
items.explanation: Lithium has a narrow therapeutic index, so levels and steady hydration and sodium are essential. A low-salt diet or dehydration raises levels dangerously, and doubling a missed dose risks toxicity.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: Fifteen minutes into a blood transfusion a patient develops fever, chills, and flank pain. What is the first action?
options: Slow the transfusion and continue at a lower rate
Begin the next unit early to maintain the schedule
Increase the rate to finish the unit more quickly
Stop the transfusion immediately and follow the transfusion reaction protocol
items.explanation: These are features of an acute transfusion reaction, so the transfusion is stopped at once and the protocol followed. Slowing, continuing or speeding up the transfusion would escalate a potentially fatal reaction.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient is prescribed subcutaneous enoxaparin. Which injection site is most appropriate?
options: The abdomen, avoiding a five centimetre area around the umbilicus
The deltoid muscle of the non-dominant arm
Directly over any existing bruise
The same fixed point every day regardless of the skin
items.explanation: Subcutaneous anticoagulants are best given into the abdominal fatty tissue, sparing the peri-umbilical area. Deltoid muscle, bruised skin and repeated identical sites raise the risk of bleeding and haematoma.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A nurse receives a medication order that is illegible and could be read as two different drugs. What is the safest practice?
options: Guess the intended drug from the patient's diagnosis
Contact the prescriber to clarify the order and document the clarification before administering
Administer the drug name that looks closest to the handwriting
Ask another patient what medicines they normally receive
items.explanation: Illegible orders must be clarified with the prescriber and the clarification documented to prevent a wrong-drug error. Guessing, choosing the closest name, or relying on another patient are all unsafe.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient is prescribed an intravenous potassium infusion. Which safety requirement is essential?
options: Give it as a fast intravenous push to correct the deficit quickly
Administer it as a large undiluted bolus without a pump
Administer at a controlled rate via a pump with appropriate dilution, never as a rapid bolus
Mix it into the patient's enteral feed
items.explanation: Rapid or concentrated potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrest, so controlled dilution and pump delivery are mandatory. Fast pushes, undiluted boluses, or enteral mixing all risk lethal hyperkalaemia or are ineffective.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient misses a dose of a prescribed oral antibiotic. What is the correct principle for managing the missed dose?
options: Double the next dose to make up the shortfall
Stop all remaining antibiotic doses
Restart the entire course from the beginning
Follow the local missed-dose policy, giving the dose if safe, and avoid doubling up
items.explanation: Missed doses are managed by policy to maintain therapy without dangerous duplication. Doubling the dose risks toxicity, stopping treatment risks relapse, and restarting the course unnecessarily prolongs therapy.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A four-year-old child is prescribed paracetamol for fever. How should the correct dose be determined?
options: By weight in kilograms using the recommended milligram per kilogram dose for age
By halving the adult dose regardless of the child's weight
By the child's age in whole years alone
By the child's height without reference to weight
items.explanation: Paediatric paracetamol is dosed by body weight to avoid under or overdosing. Halving the adult dose, or dosing by age or height alone, is inaccurate and risks hepatotoxicity or ineffective treatment.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient is prescribed methotrexate weekly, but the medication chart shows the drug to be given daily. What should the nurse do?
options: Administer it daily exactly as the chart states
Withhold the dose and clarify the frequency with the prescriber before administering
Administer both a daily and a weekly dose
Permanently withhold all of the patient's medicines
items.explanation: Daily methotrexate instead of weekly is a well-known fatal error, so administration is withheld and the frequency clarified. Following the chart or doubling the dose risks severe toxicity; withholding everything is overreach.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A nurse is about to insert an indwelling urinary catheter. Which practice best reduces the risk of infection?
options: Reuse the same catheterisation kit between several patients
Position the drainage bag above the level of the bladder
Use aseptic technique and maintain a sterile, closed drainage system
Disconnect the system several times each day for cleaning
items.explanation: Aseptic insertion with a closed system is the main defence against catheter-associated infection. Reused kits, raised drainage bags and repeated disconnections all allow organisms to ascend to the bladder.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A patient needs a peripheral intravenous cannula inserted. Which step best reduces complications?
options: Insert the cannula without cleaning the skin first
Leave the cannula in place until it stops working
Use the same insertion site for every future cannula
Perform hand hygiene, use aseptic non-touch technique, and document the insertion date for review
items.explanation: Clean technique, ANTT and documented dates enable timely review and reduce infection and phlebitis. Skipping skin preparation, leaving a failing cannula, or reusing a site all increase the risk of infection and injury.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: An immobile patient is assessed as being at risk of pressure ulcers. Which intervention is most appropriate?
options: Perform regular skin assessment with repositioning and use pressure-relieving support
Keep the patient in one position to avoid disturbing their rest
Massage reddened bony prominences vigorously each shift
Restrict fluids to reduce the need for repositioning
items.explanation: Regular assessment, repositioning and pressure-relieving surfaces are the cornerstones of prevention. Immobility, vigorous massage of damaged skin, and fluid restriction all worsen tissue breakdown and patient harm.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A patient requires blood cultures for a suspected bloodstream infection. Which action is essential for accurate results?
options: Collect the specimens only after antibiotics have been given
Collect the specimens before antibiotics are started, using aseptic technique
Wear non-sterile gloves only while collecting the sample
Delay specimen collection by 24 hours to allow the fever to settle
items.explanation: Collecting cultures before antibiotics maximises organism recovery, and aseptic technique prevents contamination. Post-antibiotic samples may be sterile, gloves alone do not ensure asepsis, and delay wastes diagnostic opportunity.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A patient has had a nasogastric tube inserted for feeding. What must be confirmed before the first feed is given?
options: That a whoosh sound is heard on auscultation alone
That the patient says the tube feels comfortable
Correct tube position using the approved pH testing method and local policy
Nothing further, because feeding can start immediately after insertion
items.explanation: Tube position must be verified by the recommended pH method before feeding to prevent feed entering the lungs. Auscultation alone and relying on patient comfort are unreliable, and feeding immediately risks pulmonary aspiration.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A hospitalised older patient is identified as being at high risk of falls. Which action best reduces the risk?
options: Apply physical restraints to keep the patient in bed
Place the call bell out of reach to discourage getting up
Raise the bed to its highest position for staff convenience
Complete a falls risk assessment and implement individualised precautions
items.explanation: Individualised precautions based on assessment are the effective falls strategy. Restraints increase injury and distress, an out-of-reach call bell removes help, and a high bed turns any fall into a serious one.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A nurse is performing hand hygiene between patient contacts. Which approach follows best practice?
options: Perform hand hygiene at the WHO five moments, including before and after every patient contact
Wash hands only when they are visibly soiled
Wear gloves instead of performing hand hygiene
Perform hand hygiene once at the start of each shift
items.explanation: The WHO five moments ensure hand hygiene at every critical point of care, which breaks transmission. Washing only when soiled, substituting gloves, or one wash per shift leaves contamination on the hands.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is prescribed an intramuscular injection. Which site and technique is appropriate for an adult?
options: Directly into an area of scarred or inflamed skin
The ventrogluteal site using an appropriately sized needle for the patient
Into the palm of the hand
Into a joint space
items.explanation: The ventrogluteal site is preferred in adults because it is relatively free of major nerves and vessels. Scarred or inflamed skin, the palm and joint spaces are unsafe and cause injury or poor absorption.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is receiving supplemental oxygen therapy on the ward. Which safety consideration is most important?
options: Allow smoking near the oxygen source as long as the patient is unwell
Oil the oxygen regulator to keep it moving smoothly
Keep oxygen away from flames and check the equipment and target saturations regularly
Set the flow as high as possible regardless of the prescribed target
items.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion, so fire risk, equipment checks and saturation targets are essential. Smoking near oxygen, oiling the regulator, and ignoring the prescribed target risk fire, contamination and oxygen toxicity.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A nurse is changing a surgical wound dressing. Which principle should guide the procedure?
options: Reuse the old dressing to reduce cost
Clean from the dirtier area towards the cleaner area
Change the dressing without wearing gloves
Use aseptic non-touch technique with a dressing appropriate to the wound type
items.explanation: ANTT and correct dressing selection protect the wound from contamination and support healing. Reusing dressings, cleaning from dirty to clean, and omitting gloves all introduce infection and cross-contamination.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A nurse must complete a patient's fluid balance record over a shift. Which documentation is correct?
options: Record all measured intake and output accurately, including losses required by protocol
Record only the fluids the patient drinks
Estimate the urine output roughly without measuring it
Record entries only when the doctor requests a review
items.explanation: Accurate intake and output recording underpins safe fluid management and early detection of imbalance. Recording only drinks, estimating output, or charting on request only conceals deterioration and misleads the team.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A patient with a tracheostomy needs airway suctioning. Which approach is safest?
options: Suction continuously for a full minute without supplemental oxygen
Pre-oxygenate, use sterile technique, and limit each suction pass according to policy
Use the same suction catheter for every patient on the unit
Suction only while the patient is deeply asleep
items.explanation: Pre-oxygenation, sterility and brief suction passes minimise hypoxaemia and infection. Prolonged suctioning without oxygen causes desaturation, shared catheters spread organisms, and suctioning a sleeping patient is unsafe.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A nurse begins a blood transfusion. Why should the nurse stay with the patient for the first fifteen minutes?
options: To complete the paperwork while waiting
To save time on the next nursing task
To observe for signs of an acute transfusion reaction
To adjust the patient's diet plan for the day
items.explanation: Most acute transfusion reactions occur early, so direct observation in the first minutes allows immediate detection and response. Paperwork, task efficiency and diet planning do not address the patient's immediate safety.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is starting a 24-hour urine collection for investigation. What instruction is correct?
options: Collect only the first sample of the day and discard the rest
Include any toilet water from the collection container
Store the container at room temperature for the whole day
Discard the first void, then collect all urine for the full period and store it as advised
items.explanation: A complete collection starts after discarding the first void and includes all subsequent urine stored correctly. Partial collection, added toilet water, or incorrect storage invalidates the result and may misdirect treatment.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A bedbound patient requires repositioning to prevent complications of immobility. How often should this normally occur?
options: At least every two hours or according to the individualised turning schedule
Once at the beginning of each shift
Only when the patient complains of discomfort
Once every twenty-four hours
items.explanation: Regular repositioning at roughly two-hourly intervals, tailored to the patient, protects skin and circulation. Once per shift, complaint-driven, or daily turning allows pressure damage and respiratory complications to develop.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Patient Care and Procedures

items.stem: A nurse realises that the wrong dose of a medicine was given to a patient. What is the correct professional action?
options: Conceal the error to avoid any disciplinary consequence
Report the error promptly, monitor the patient, and complete an incident report
Blame a colleague who was not involved
Delay reporting the error until the end of the month
items.explanation: Prompt reporting and patient monitoring are professional duties that protect the patient and improve safety. Concealment, shifting blame and delay are dishonest, harm the patient, and breach professional standards.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A competent adult refuses a blood transfusion that the clinical team believes is life-saving. What should the practitioner do?
options: Proceed with the transfusion against the patient's expressed wishes
Ignore the refusal and treat as planned
Respect the informed refusal and document the discussion and capacity assessment
Ask a relative to sign consent in place of the patient
items.explanation: A competent adult has the right to refuse treatment even when it is life-saving, and the decision must be documented. Proceeding against the refusal is battery, ignoring it is unlawful, and a relative cannot consent for a competent adult.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A patient's relative asks the nurse for confidential details of the patient's diagnosis, and the patient has not consented to disclosure. What should the nurse do?
options: Provide the details because the relative is family
Give the relative a copy of the full medical record
Discuss the diagnosis freely in the public waiting area
Decline to share confidential information without consent, except where disclosure is legally permitted
items.explanation: Confidentiality belongs to the patient, so information is not shared with relatives without consent or a legal basis. Assuming family access, releasing records, or discussing details publicly all breach patient privacy and the law.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A practitioner must obtain informed consent for a procedure. What does valid informed consent require?
options: Explanation of the procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives in a language the patient understands, with capacity present
A signature collected without any explanation of the procedure
A minor signing on behalf of an adult patient
Reliance on a general ward consent form with no discussion
items.explanation: Informed consent requires capacity, adequate understandable information, and voluntary agreement. Silent signatures, a minor consenting for an adult, or a generic form without discussion do not constitute valid consent.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A nurse suspects that a colleague is practising while impaired by alcohol. What is the professional duty?
options: Ignore it to avoid causing a conflict on the unit
Report the concern through the appropriate channels to protect patient safety
Quietly cover for the colleague during the shift
Share the suspicion as gossip with other staff
items.explanation: Patient safety takes priority, so an impaired colleague must be reported through the proper channels. Ignoring, covering, or gossiping about the concern leaves patients at risk and fails professional accountability.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A patient is assessed as lacking the capacity to make a particular treatment decision. What is the appropriate approach?
options: Make decisions based solely on the cost of treatment
Disregard any previously expressed wishes of the patient
Act in the patient's best interests following the law and local policy, involving relevant parties
Delay all care indefinitely until the patient regains capacity
items.explanation: When capacity is absent, decisions follow the best-interests framework in law and policy, considering prior wishes. Cost-only decisions, ignoring previous preferences, and indefinite delay all fail the duty of care.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A practitioner is asked to falsify a patient's clinical record to support an insurance claim. What should the practitioner do?
options: Falsify the record to help the patient obtain the claim
Alter the record but leave it unsigned
Ask a colleague to falsify the record instead
Refuse to falsify the record and report the request through the appropriate channel
items.explanation: Falsifying clinical records is fraud that breaches professional and legal duties, so the request must be refused and reported. Doing it directly or via a colleague, or altering it unsigned, remains dishonest and unlawful.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: Which statement best describes the ethical principle of non-maleficence in clinical practice?
options: The duty to avoid causing harm to the patient
The duty to maximise benefits for the patient
The duty to respect autonomy above all other principles
The duty to distribute resources equally across all patients
items.explanation: Non-maleficence is the obligation to avoid harm. Maximising benefit describes beneficence, respecting autonomy describes autonomy, and fair resource allocation describes justice, so the other options name different principles.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A patient asks to see their own medical records. Under the applicable law, what should the practitioner do?
options: Refuse every request for records automatically
Facilitate the patient's lawful access to their records following the organisation's process
Destroy the records so they cannot be released
Allow access only if a doctor agrees informally, with no process
items.explanation: Patients have a legal right of access to their records, so the organisation's access process should be followed. Automatic refusal, destruction of records, or an informal undocumented arrangement breaches that right and the law.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A healthcare worker posts a patient's photograph on social media without consent, even though no name is shown. This action is a breach of what?
options: Only the hospital dress code
Nothing, because the patient's name was not displayed
Patient confidentiality and privacy
A minor administrative rule with no ethical weight
items.explanation: Identifiable images are personal health information, so sharing them without consent breaches confidentiality and privacy even without a name. Dress code, the absence of a name, and administrative framing all miss the ethical and legal breach.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A competent patient asks directly about a diagnosis that carries a poor prognosis. How should the clinical team respond?
options: Always withhold the truth to protect the patient from distress
Ask the family to decide and never tell the patient
Give false reassurance to keep the patient calm
Provide truthful information in a sensitive manner, respecting the patient's wishes about how much to know
items.explanation: Truthful, sensitive disclosure respects autonomy and the patient's right to know, tailored to their wishes. Withholding the truth, deferring entirely to the family, or giving false reassurance undermines trust and informed decision-making.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A nurse is asked to perform a procedure that is outside their scope of practice and training. What should the nurse do?
options: Decline the task and escalate, working only within their competence and scope
Perform the procedure anyway without any training or supervision
Delegate the procedure to an unqualified assistant
Sign the documentation without actually performing the procedure
items.explanation: Practitioners must work within their competence and scope, so an out-of-scope task is declined and escalated. Proceeding untrained, delegating to an unqualified person, or falsifying documentation all endanger patients and breach standards.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: Which action best demonstrates the ethical principle of justice in healthcare delivery?
options: Giving preferential treatment to wealthier patients
Treating patients fairly and allocating resources without discrimination
Ignoring patients' cultural and language needs
Prioritising staff convenience over patient needs
items.explanation: Justice requires fairness, equity and non-discrimination in care and resource allocation. Preferential treatment by wealth, ignoring cultural needs, or privileging staff convenience all violate the principle of justice.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A practitioner discloses a patient's information to the public health authority because a notifiable disease must be reported by law. How should this be regarded?
options: As a criminal act that must always be hidden
As a breach that should never be recorded
As permitted, because the law requires disclosure for public safety
As allowed only if the patient gives written permission in every case
items.explanation: Statutory reporting of notifiable diseases is a lawful, required disclosure that overrides ordinary confidentiality in the public interest. Treating it as criminal, concealing it, or requiring consent in every case misunderstands the legal duty.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics

items.stem: A patient wants to document an advance directive about their future care. What is the appropriate response from the practitioner?
options: Tell the patient that an advance directive has no value
Complete the document on the patient's behalf without any discussion
Discard the document as an unnecessary formality
Support the patient in documenting their wishes following the legal and policy requirements
items.explanation: Advance directives let patients record future care preferences and should be supported within the legal framework. Dismissing their value, completing it without the patient, or discarding it denies the patient autonomy and breaches policy.
items.reference: MOH UAE Examination Syllabus - Medical Law and Ethics
